Galiano Island Marine animals of Galiano Island (1893–2021) A catalogue of the marine animals reported from the waters around Galiano Island, from sponges and worms to fishes and marine mammals, bringing together historical collections and published reports with the community science observations gathered by the Biodiversity Galiano project since 2016. Records distinguish historical reports that have since been confirmed, those that remain unconfirmed, and species newly reported for the island. View dataset →
Data paper: Simon et al. (2022), Biodiversity Data Journal 10: e76050
We respectfully acknowledge that this work takes place within the traditional territories of the Penelakut, Hwlitsum and Tsawwassen First Nations, among other Hul’qumi’num-speaking Coast Salish peoples, who have cared for these lands and waters since time immemorial.
Salish Sea Diatoms of the Salish Sea (1866–2026) A catalogue of marine diatom occurrences across the Salish Sea, consolidating records from the published literature, morphological study of samples and molecular (DNA metabarcoding) surveys. Together, these records document the region’s diatom flora and how knowledge of it has accumulated since the first reports in 1866. View dataset →
Data paper: Webber et al. (2026), Biodiversity Data Journal 14: e189060

Our approach to detecting biodiversity change is documented in the Protocol for the Detection of Extirpation, which walks through our framework for inferring local extinction using a tutorial dataset from Galiano Island. The protocol is described in full in our article in Plants, People, Planet. Aspects of this protocol have been adapted in the bioReportR framework, with examples presented here for the Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere and Saanich Peninsula.
Xetthecum: a learning journey documents the Xetthecum ecocultural mapping pilot at Retreat Cove, Galiano Island, from early research to community engagement.

Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Flora of Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound A map-based report on the vascular plant diversity of the Átl’ḵa7tsem/Howe Sound Biosphere Region, drawing on historical collections and community science observations to relate the region’s plants to biogeoclimatic zones and protected areas, map their status, track species that have not been reported in recent decades, and recognise the contributors whose records make this work possible. Visit project site →
We respectfully acknowledge that this work takes place on the unceded territory of the Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw (Squamish Nation), who have cared for these lands and waters since time immemorial.
Galiano Island Protocol for the Detection of Extirpation Developed on Galiano Island, this protocol for detecting local extinction, or extirpation, combines historical specimens, community science observations and targeted searches. Weighing the search effort spent in each species' historical and potential habitat, the protocol tests the hypothesis that a population has been lost, in line with IUCN extinction criteria. Published in Plants, People, Planet. Visit project site →
We respectfully acknowledge that this work takes place within the traditional territories of the Penelakut, Hwlitsum and Tsawwassen First Nations, among other Hul’qumi’num-speaking Coast Salish peoples, who have cared for these lands and waters since time immemorial.
Xetthecum Ecocultural Mapping Pilot An initiative weaving together Indigenous ways of knowing and Western ecological science into an ecocultural map of Retreat Cove (Xetthecum in the Hul’qumi’num language), Galiano Island. Created in partnership with Indigenous and non-Indigenous collaborators, this participatory mapping program brings together historical and contemporary biodiversity data, terrestrial ecosystem mapping, written and spoken Hul’qumi’num, and stories of place, fostering a holistic approach to shle’muxun—“guardian of the land,” or “stewardship,” in Hul’qumi’num. Visit project site →
Documentation: Xetthecum: a learning journey
We respectfully acknowledge that this work takes place within the traditional territories of the Penelakut, Hwlitsum and Tsawwassen First Nations, among other Hul’qumi’num-speaking Coast Salish peoples, who have cared for these lands and waters since time immemorial. This work is guided by the Indigenous-led Whiteswan Environmental through its Spirit of the Sxwo’le (SOS) Coalition, a cross-cultural community of practice grounded in protocols of respect and reciprocity. We are grateful for funding provided by the Indigenous Watersheds Initiative, the Inclusive Design Research Centre, the Southern Gulf Islands Community Resource Centre, and the Capital Regional District in support of this ongoing ecocultural mapping initiative.
W̱SÁNEĆ/Saanich Peninsula Flora of W̱SÁNEĆ/Saanich Peninsula An analysis of the vascular plant flora of the Saanich Peninsula, drawing on historical collections and community science observations to map the status of the region’s plants, track species that have not been reported in recent decades, and recognise the contributors whose records make this work possible. This work builds on the foundation of Harvey Janszen’s revisions of Szczawinski and Harrison’s (1972) Flora of the Saanich Peninsula through ongoing data curation involving a community of naturalists in the Salish Sea. Visit project site →
We respectfully acknowledge that this work takes place within the territories of the W̱SÁNEĆ (Saanich) people, who have cared for these lands and waters since time immemorial. This project is undertaken in partnership with Paige Erickson-Mcgee of Habitat Acquisition Trust and Cara Gibson of Swan Lake Nature Sanctuary. We especially thank Ian Cruickshank, Matt Fairbarns, Frank Lomer, Terry Ludwar, Andy MacKinnon, Adam Martin, Emma Menchions, James Miskelly, and Kristen Miskelly for their direct contributions. We are grateful for funding provided by the Sitka Foundation, the Capital Regional District, Nature Victoria, and Keefer Ecological Services Ltd. in support of this project.
